blindSummary:
This country combines relatively low everyday risk for visitors with one of the region's most restrictive legal-gender-recognition situations. The civil code grants the right to medically change gender in principle, but there has been no legal framework regulating the procedure for 17 years — a deadlock the Constitutional Court refused to resolve in September 2025, perpetuating what the regional human-rights court has called severe legal uncertainty.

Socially, a conservative climate is well documented: an MP called LGBT people "degenerated" and "spreading diseases" (his immunity was revoked), "traditional family values" groups disrupt peaceful protests, the parliamentary ombudsperson found police failed to guarantee the LGBT community's right to assembly, and trans people report systemic workplace harassment — open ridicule, isolation, and psychological abuse. A "protection of minors" law limits dissemination of LGBT information (a 2024 Constitutional Court ruling weakened its same-sex-family provision). There is no criminalisation, and the 2024 pride event drew 15,000 people.
blindOutOfScope: No trans-specific travel advisory; ordinary crime is low.
blindSourceSummaries: National LGBT-rights organisation news (Sept 2025): the Constitutional Court refused to address this country's 18-year trans-rights gap - a significant setback; the civil code grants unmarried adults the right to medically change gender, but implementing legislation has never been adopted, leaving trans people in legal limbo.

National LGBT-rights organisation news (Aug 2025): could courts finally end 17 years of legal limbo for transgender rights? - a regional district court sitting in a provincial city suspended a civil case on amending civil-status gender documents and referred the question of the laws' compliance with the constitution to the Constitutional Court.

Public broadcaster (Sept 2025): this country's Constitutional Court declined to examine a lower court's request to review the absence of legal provisions allowing trans people to change gender markers and personal identification codes in official documents.
Public broadcaster (May 2025): trans people in this country detail workplace harassment - open ridicule, isolation and psychological abuse; systemic labour-market discrimination per experts.

National LGBT-rights organisation news (April 2024): the parliamentary ombudsperson found that police failed to guarantee the LGBT community's right to peaceful assembly - inadequate police response to hostile provocateurs at an LGBT organisation's gathering; recommended measures to guarantee effective assembly rights.

National equality-body report (2024), summary of the second national review of the situation of transgender people (after 2019): covers public attitudes, the legal framework, document changes, healthcare barriers, labour-market discrimination, data protection and negative public attitudes; notes the lack of a legal framework and of a strategic approach.

Regional LGBT-rights organisation's annual review 2025 (covering 2024), chapter on this country: systemic lack of targeted LGBTI hate-crime victim support; LGBTI asylum seekers from a third country granted protection after a four-year wait, with dire camp conditions and a psychologist convicted of coercing asylum seekers into sexual acts; prosecution of a former MP for anti-LGBTI ridicule complicated by his immunity as a member of the supranational union's parliament.

LGBTQ news outlet (Sept 2013): this country's parliament to consider five anti-gay and anti-trans bills - a ban on gender reassignment (defining gender as genetically determined from the moment of conception), a same-sex adoption ban, fines of up to 1,800 units of local currency for organisers of events denigrating the constitutional moral values, and legalisation of anti-gay speech.

LGBTQ news outlet (July 2009): this country's parliament passed a 'protection of minors' law banning information on homosexuality in schools and media accessible to minors - a promotion-style clause of a type first seen in another country - overriding the president's veto 87-6; an international human-rights organisation called it a huge step backwards.
blindLocalsOnly: The 17-year legal-gender-recognition deadlock and the workplace-harassment documentation are resident-facing; the 'protection of minors' dissemination law is a resident/climate signal.
